text:
morgan: hit a flaky behavior in staging: when an upstream is evicted mid-stream (OOM or preempt) the client sometimes gets a short chunk of text then a silent connection close. UI spins or shows gibberish.

hailey: saw that too. current proxy sends a hard reset and we lose any chance to tell clients "this was partial but resumable".

vikram: can we standardize a small "evict handshake" that always attempts to signal progress before closing? two pieces: 1) a control-frame (inline JSON chunk) fallback for transports without trailers, and 2) a compact resume token (stateless by default) so clients can retry.

tara: agree. control-frame sketch (inline chunk for HTTP/1 or clients that don't support trailers):
```
{"_rw_evict":{"id":"c0d1f2","offset":2912,"v":"1","reason":"preempt","resume":true,"ttl":30}}
```
for HTTP/2+ prefer trailers:
```
x-rw-evict-id: c0d1f2
x-rw-offset: 2912
x-rw-resume: true
grpc-status: 8
```

morgan: stateless resume token idea: signed compact blob with fields {v, route, offset, ttl, fingerprint} base64url-encoded. gateway validates signature; no per-stream retention needed. stateful mode available as opt-in for enterprise customers who want exact KV cache resume.

hailey: tradeoffs: stateless reduces memory but replay cost increases; stateful reduces replay but consumes MB-seconds. need admission control: per-tenant resume mb-second quota and an eviction policy. if quota exhausted, still emit control-frame but `resume=false`.

vikram: route config knobs proposal: `resume_mode: stateless|stateful|off`, `checkpoint_every_tokens: 128`, `resume_ttl_seconds: 30`, `resume_admission_mb_seconds: 1000` (tenant-scoped). default = stateless.

tara: client flow: on control-frame present && resume==true -> UI shows "partial result (resume available)". clicking retry sends header `x-rw-resume: <token-or-id>`. gateway validates token or looks up state and routes to resume handler or fallback variant `model-short`. if missing -> respond with `x-rw-resume-fallback: true`.

morgan: metrics: `edge.evict.control_emitted`, `edge.evict.resume_issued`, `edge.evict.resume_used`, `edge.evict.resume_miss`, `edge.evict.fallback_rate`. alert: `EVICT_FALLBACK_RATE > 5% for 10m`.

hailey: billing: tokens emitted before evict are billed normally. resumed tokens billed to the retrying request. if gateway replays tokens server-side (stateful rehydrate) record `edge.resume.replay_ms` as compute-overhead and bill separately. document expectation that replay costs may be charged.

vikram: security: token MUST NOT contain raw prompt or PII. only include short fingerprint/hash. sign tokens with rotating gateway keys. include `v` for schema version. add key-rotation doc.

tara: SDK work: add ResumeManager that parses both control-frame inline JSON and trailers and exposes api `parseResume(meta) -> {canResume, token}` and `resume(token)` helper. Node + Python SDKs to ship. small client test harness to simulate mid-stream RST and validate resume UX.

morgan: tests: add chaos harness `chaos/evict-handshake` that injects soft/hard evicts at different offsets, assert clients get either control-frame or clear error, and that resume flow returns coherent continuations within allowed checkpoint drift. add fuzz across HTTP/1, HTTP/2, and H3.

hailey: runbook snippet: "If EVICT_FALLBACK_RATE > 5%: check resume-store util, tenant mb-second usage, checkpoint frequency; consider increasing checkpoint_every_tokens or enabling stateful mode for affected tenant."

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: gateway/edge-proxy v1.50.0 -> canary (us-east-1) :rocket:

morgan: i'll write RFC with the handshake contract, token schema (v1), route knobs, billing implications, SDK contract, testplan, and rollout gating. link when ready.

vikram: +1. let's gate behind feature-flag `edge.evict.handshake.v1` and collect the new metrics before wide rollout.

deploy-bot: canary deploy succeeded: gateway/edge-proxy v1.50.0 -> 2/3 hosts (us-east-1) succeeded.
